title: The Generation Effect: Producing Beats Receiving
explainer: Distinct from the testing effect (the benefit of retrieval practice), the generation effect — documented by Norman Slamecka and Peter Graf in the late 1970s — shows that information a learner actively produces, such as completing, paraphrasing, or explaining it in their own words, is remembered better than information merely read. Explaining a topic to someone else forces this kind of active generation rather than passive recognition, which is a separate mechanism from simply re-testing yourself on the same material.
